written: 2026-11-20, after SeedLM-20, before any SeedLM-21 coder was trained
motivation: Of the parent -> child links (edges) in held-out teacher programs that neither the 100,000 synthetic library programs nor any training program has, 9 of 98 join two library operators; the rest touch a Python node (26 are a Python node over a library operator). In the held-out development one-liners beyond the engine none of the 23 joins two operators (reports/seedlm/pysynth_coverage.json)
The coder's synthetic rows (300,000) hold library operators only; Python nodes reach it only through a few thousand teacher-written programs

SeedLM-6's grafts covered the new pieces of 7 of 77 held-out new-combination programs and, repeated over three seeds (SeedLM-12), lowered the surprisal of new-edge tokens without writing more of those programs correctly
hypothesis: Programs that mix Python nodes with library operators at scale teach the coder to build the Python-node junctions held-out programs need, so it writes more held-out programs that hold a new combination
data: mylittlellm/seedlm/pysynth.py over the input cases of the training teacher tasks and variants: 30,000 programs (seed 0), library operators drawn in proportion to the square root of their use in training programs. The draw ('sqrt') was chosen among three ('all', 'training', 'sqrt') on a proxy built from training programs only (five parts of the training teacher tasks and variants, each part's new edges against the synthetic programs and the other training programs: covered programs 232, 253, 283 of 970; reports/seedlm/pysynth_proxy_*.json). Rows are described like the grafts (mylittlellm/seedlm/pyx_words.py), three cases per program
coverage_before_training: measured once for the chosen settings: held-out teacher programs with a new edge 65, all new edges covered 15; new edges 98, covered 31. Beyond: 7 programs, 1 fully covered; 23 edges, 9 covered (reports/seedlm/pysynth_coverage.json)
arm: three post-coders s21-y1, s21-y2, s21-y3: scripts/seedlm4_train.py --name s21-y<seed> --minutes 40 --d-model 320 --layers 8 --heads 10 --views 3 --seed <seed> --variant-share 0.1 --pysynth-share 0.15 --pysynth-count 30000 --pysynth-library sqrt, seeds 1, 2, 3; nothing else runs while they train
control: s12-a1, s12-a2, s12-a3 (SeedLM-12: the same arguments without --pysynth-share)
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks whose own program holds a token, edge or twig that neither the synthetic library programs nor any training program has (77 of 139; scripts/seedlm21_compare.py): the first program at beam width 32 that reproduces the visible example is correct on every case (SeedLM-15's cache). Mean of the three arm coders against the controls' (20, 21, 23: 21.33). Supported if the arm's mean is at least 25.33 (+4); not supported if at most 22.33 (+1); inconclusive otherwise
protection: held-out teacher tasks whose pieces are all seen (62; controls 39, 38, 39): the arm's mean may not be more than 3 below the controls' 38.67, or the result is reported as a trade, not a gain
secondary_measures: teacher-program tokens at new edges: mean nats and share ranked first (scripts/seedlm5_fragments.py --model; controls 4.31, 4.51, 3.63 nats on held-out teacher programs, 8.65, 8.81, 7.30 on beyond)
the vote of all twenty-four cached coders on the development fifth and the teacher tasks (scripts/seedlm16_occam.py; twenty-one coders 64.63 and 71.23)
